observations.disposition_note: Treated as a contractual restriction (covenant), not a payment; the conditional share reflects that the payout is only triggered if new debt is added.

The two balances describe one obligation family (Shopify/WebBank sales-linked merchant loans subject to the same payoff covenant); each is quoted verbatim and checked separately, so combining them does not blur scope.
The balance is context identifying the loan; the checkable claim is the single $600,000 2024 bucket. The VitBest row link rests on the matching $2,920,824 amount and is marked as an inference.

The source states both dates' balances in one sentence as a single figure; the checkable claim is that the balance did not change, which is what establishes that the 2024 bucket was unpaid at June 30, 2024.
Amount and purpose are stated in a single clause of the source and are checked together; this is one fact about one cash pool.
"No further cash is owed" follows directly from "paid in full"; it restates the same fact, not an independent claim.
The source reports the draw and the repayment in one sentence as the net activity on a single note; splitting them would lose the net context. Both are quoted verbatim.
The former supplier is identified as Atrium through the Note 13 cross-reference (fnd_003); marked inference.

The consequence restates the quoted covenant ('Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out KTI first') and applies it to the proposed advance, which is debt by definition. No further factual claim is made.
The ruling's content and its lack of a payment term are one fact about one procedural decision: the quoted disposition addresses only pleading counts, so no payment obligation arises from it.
One source sentence pair describing the same Knight loan's balance, rate and covenant, quoted verbatim. It is used only for inventory context and scope, not as the basis of a cash effect.

findings.proposition: The Atrium litigation was settled in December 2023 by a contractual settlement agreement that created a $5,450,000 settlement loan payable (5% interest). Its outstanding balance was $4,802,445 at both December 31, 2023 and June 30, 2024, so no principal was paid in H1 2024. The disclosed schedule requires $2,000,000 in 2024, $2,000,000 in 2025 and $802,445 in 2026, so the full $2,000,000 2024 bucket remained unpaid at June 30, 2024. Payments between July 1 and August 13, 2024 are not disclosed. Linking the "Atrium" notes-payable row to this loan relies on the matching $4,802,445 balance and the Note 13 cross-reference, so the link is an inference.

findings.proposition: Under the amended Knight Therapeutics consolidated loan (finalized June 2024), the loan is senior secured against all current and future assets of Synergy and its subsidiaries, and "Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying out KTI first". A default on third-party debt automatically puts the Knight loan in default, and a Knight default cross-defaults the Sanders modification loan. The evidence does not show any Knight consent to additional debt.

There is a cross -default clause in the agreement which states that if Knight triggers an event of default on its own loan facility, this loan will also be under default.
